prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: shopping around at renewal. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 0)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a member says they are shopping around at renewal, I should separate genuine cover comparison from a simple price check, because the cheapest includes the same accidental damage, windscreen, personal possessions and legal cover, because differences in scope can make like-for-like pricing impossible."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a market."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the member is undecided, I should explain that continuity can help if they have specialist cover or a complicated claim history, but I should not imply and protected no claims bonus are included, because those items can swing the real value more than the headline premium."},{"type":"observation","content":"When comparing home renewals, I should look for changes in escape of water terms, trace and access limits, and contents away from home cover, because these are commonly missed when members focus only on the monthly price."},{"type":"preference","content":"When a member is shopping around because service has been poor, I should note the complaint driver separately from the price driver, because a clear service issue may mean they simply want a smoother claims experience next year."},{"type":"fact","content":"When the renewal market is tight after storm or theft activity in the area, I should expect fewer
